phaseHajj1Description: Hajj is the fifth pillar of Islam and the greatest journey a Muslim can undertake in their lifetime. It is obligatory once in a lifetime for every Muslim who is physically and financially able. You are about to walk in the footsteps of Ibrahim عليه السلام, Hajar, Ismail عليه السلام and the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ himself. Millions of Muslims from every corner of the earth gather as one — no kings, no servants, no rich, no poor — all equal before Allah in two white sheets. Prepare your heart as much as your body. This journey will change you forever.
phaseHajj1Dua1Translation: Here I am O Allah, for Hajj
phaseHajj1Dua2Title: Talbiyah — recite continuously until the stoning of Jamarat
phaseHajj1Dua2Translation: Here I am O Allah, here I am. Here I am, You have no partner, here I am. Verily all praise, grace and sovereignty belong to You. You have no partner
phaseHajj1Dua3Translation: O Allah I intend to perform Hajj so make it easy for me and accept it from me
phaseHajj1Dua4Translation: O Allah make it an accepted Hajj, an appreciated effort and a forgiven sin
phaseHajj1Dua5Title: Bonus — dua for ease throughout Hajj
phaseHajj1Dua5Translation: O Allah make it easy and do not make it difficult and complete it with goodness
phaseHajj1Dua6Title: Bonus — dua of Ibrahim عليه السلام when he called people to Hajj
phaseHajj1Dua6Translation: Our Lord make us both submissive to You and from our descendants a nation submissive to You. Show us our rites of worship and accept our repentance. Indeed You are the Ever-Relenting the Most Merciful
phaseHajj1FemaleNote: Women must be accompanied by a Mahram (husband or male relative) for Hajj — this is an Islamic requirement not a logistical suggestion. Women wear their normal modest clothing — no special Ihram garment. Women do not cover the face or hands during Ihram. Women in their menstrual cycle still enter Ihram and perform all rituals except Tawaf — they wait until they are pure before performing Tawaf. Do not let your cycle cause you anxiety — many women experience this and the scholars have addressed it comprehensively. Women recite Talbiyah quietly.
phaseHajj1Step1: Learn the complete rituals of Hajj before you go — ignorance leads to mistakes that may require expiation
phaseHajj1Step10: Make the Niyyah for Hajj at the Miqat — say it aloud
phaseHajj1Step11: Begin reciting the Talbiyah — men loudly, women quietly — and do not stop until you stone the Jamarat on Eid day
phaseHajj1Step2: Make sincere Tawbah (repentance) before Hajj — come to Allah's house with a clean heart
phaseHajj1Step3: Write your will before departing — this is a Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ before any long journey
phaseHajj1Step4: Trim nails, remove unwanted body hair and prepare the body before Ghusl
phaseHajj1Step5: Perform Ghusl with the intention of Ihram — this is Sunnah even for women in their menstrual cycle
phaseHajj1Step6: Men apply perfume to the body before wearing Ihram — not to the garments themselves
phaseHajj1Step7: Men wear two white unstitched sheets — Izar (lower) and Rida (upper). No underwear or stitched clothing
phaseHajj1Step8: Women wear their normal modest clothing in any colour — no special garment required
phaseHajj1Step9: Pray 2 rakats of Ihram sunnah prayer — Surah Al-Kafirun in the first rakat and Al-Ikhlas in the second
phaseHajj1Tip1: Hajj is physically one of the most demanding acts of worship — train your body before you go. Walk long distances in the months before Hajj
phaseHajj1Tip10: The reward of a Mabrur (accepted) Hajj is nothing but Jannah — there is no greater bargain
phaseHajj1Tip2: The Prophet ﷺ said — whoever performs Hajj without committing obscenity or sin returns like the day his mother gave birth to him
phaseHajj1Tip3: Hajj is only accepted from those who have fulfilled the rights of others — pay your debts, ask forgiveness from those you have wronged before you leave
phaseHajj1Tip4: Pack light — you will be moving between multiple locations. Comfort is more important than luxury
phaseHajj1Tip5: Wear comfortable shoes — you will walk enormous distances. Break in your shoes before Hajj
phaseHajj1Tip6: Bring a small notebook — write your duas, the names of people who asked you to make dua for them, and your reflections each day
phaseHajj1Tip7: The Talbiyah is the heartbeat of Hajj — recite it at every moment, especially when going uphill, downhill, boarding transport or meeting other pilgrims
phaseHajj1Tip8: Join a reputable Hajj group with a knowledgeable scholar who can guide you through the rituals
phaseHajj1Tip9: Be patient with crowds, heat and difficulty — every hardship during Hajj is expiation for sins
phaseHajj2Description: Arriving in Makkah for Hajj is different from arriving for Umrah. The city is at its most alive — millions of pilgrims from every nation on earth have gathered in one place answering the call of Ibrahim عليه السلام. The energy is unlike anything you will ever experience. Your first task upon arriving is Tawaf Al-Qudum — the arrival Tawaf — which is a Sunnah greeting of the Masjid Al-Haram. Use every moment in Makkah before the main days of Hajj to worship, rest and prepare spiritually.
phaseHajj2Dua1Translation: O Allah this is Your sanctuary and Your place of safety, so forbid my flesh to the Hellfire and keep me safe from Your punishment on the day You resurrect Your servants
phaseHajj2Dua2Title: Dua upon first seeing the Kaaba
phaseHajj2Dua2Translation: O Allah You are Peace and from You comes peace, so greet us our Lord with peace
phaseHajj2Dua3Translation: O Allah I ask You for beneficial knowledge, abundant provision and cure from every disease
phaseHajj2Dua4Title: Bonus — dua for the days ahead
phaseHajj2Dua4Translation: O Allah help me to remember You, to be grateful to You and to worship You in the best manner
phaseHajj2Dua5Title: Bonus — dua when entering the Haram
phaseHajj2Dua5Translation: In the name of Allah and peace and blessings upon the Messenger of Allah. O Allah forgive my sins and open for me the gates of Your mercy
phaseHajj2FemaleNote: Women should stay close to their Mahram at all times in the crowded Haram. Women do not perform Idtiba or Raml during Tawaf Al-Qudum — walk at a normal pace. Women should use the less crowded times to perform Tawaf — after Fajr and late at night. Women in their menstrual cycle skip Tawaf Al-Qudum and wait until they are pure — this does not affect the validity of their Hajj.
phaseHajj2Step1: Enter Makkah reciting the dua for entering a city — be in a state of wudu if possible
phaseHajj2Step10: Spend your time in the Haram in worship — Tawaf, Quran, dua and dhikr
phaseHajj2Step11: Familiarise yourself with the layout of the Haram, the routes to Mina, Arafah and Muzdalifah
phaseHajj2Step2: Head to Masjid Al-Haram and enter with your right foot reciting the masjid entry dua
phaseHajj2Step3: When the Kaaba first comes into view — stop, raise your hands and make as much dua as possible. This is one of the most powerful moments for dua acceptance
phaseHajj2Step4: Perform Tawaf Al-Qudum (arrival Tawaf) — 7 rounds around the Kaaba. This is Sunnah for those performing Hajj Qiran or Ifrad
phaseHajj2Step5: Those performing Hajj Tamattu who already completed Umrah do not need to perform Tawaf Al-Qudum
phaseHajj2Step6: After Tawaf pray 2 rakats behind Maqam Ibrahim
phaseHajj2Step7: Drink Zamzam water making dua while drinking
phaseHajj2Step8: Perform Sa'i if you are performing Hajj Qiran or Ifrad — those doing Tamattu already completed Sa'i during Umrah
phaseHajj2Step9: Settle in your accommodation and rest — the hardest days begin on the 8th of Dhul Hijjah
phaseHajj2Tip1: Use the days before the 8th of Dhul Hijjah wisely — do as much Tawaf as possible while you still can move freely
phaseHajj2Tip2: The Haram will become extremely crowded as Hajj days approach — learn the layout early
phaseHajj2Tip3: Rest as much as possible — sleep is worship during Hajj when it is to prepare for the rituals
phaseHajj2Tip4: There are three types of Hajj — Tamattu (most common, perform Umrah first then Hajj), Qiran (Umrah and Hajj together without exiting Ihram) and Ifrad (Hajj only). Know which one you are performing
phaseHajj2Tip5: Hajj Tamattu requires a sacrifice (Hady) — arrange this in advance through your Hajj group or an authorised service
phaseHajj2Tip6: Eat well and stay hydrated — the heat in Makkah during Hajj season can be extreme
phaseHajj2Tip7: Keep your Hajj documents, passport and important items in a secure pouch worn under your Ihram
phaseHajj2Tip8: Memorise or save the address of your accommodation — it is easy to get lost in the crowds
phaseHajj3Description: The 8th of Dhul Hijjah is called Yawm Al-Tarwiyah — the Day of Quenching Thirst — named after the day when pilgrims historically filled their water vessels in preparation for the journey to Arafah. This is the day Hajj truly begins. You leave the comforts of Makkah and move to Mina — a valley of white tents stretching as far as the eye can see. It is a powerful reminder that this world is temporary — you are a traveller passing through. Spend this night in worship and prepare your heart and your duas for the greatest day of the year — the Day of Arafah.
phaseHajj3Dua1Title: Niyyah for Hajj when re-entering Ihram (Tamattu pilgrims)
phaseHajj3Dua1Translation: Here I am O Allah, for Hajj
phaseHajj3Dua2Translation: Here I am O Allah, here I am. Here I am, You have no partner, here I am. Verily all praise, grace and sovereignty belong to You. You have no partner
phaseHajj3Dua3Translation: O Allah this is Mina so bestow upon me what You have bestowed upon Your close friends
phaseHajj3Dua4Title: Dua before sleeping — preparing for Arafah
phaseHajj3Dua4Translation: O Allah I ask You for pardon and well-being in this world and the next
phaseHajj3Dua5Title: Bonus — dua of Ibrahim عليه السلام who walked this same path
phaseHajj3Dua5Translation: My Lord make me one who establishes prayer and from my descendants. Our Lord and accept my supplication
phaseHajj3Dua6Title: Bonus — dua for the night in Mina
phaseHajj3Dua6Translation: Glory be to You O Allah and with Your praise I bear witness that there is no god but You I seek Your forgiveness and repent to You
phaseHajj3FemaleNote: Women should stay within the tent and close to their Mahram during the night in Mina. The tents are separated by gender in most Hajj groups. Women in their menstrual cycle perform all rituals in Mina normally — there is no Tawaf required at this stage. Make the most of the night in Mina — recite Quran, make dhikr and prepare your personal duas for Arafah. The night before Arafah is precious — do not waste it on sleep alone.
phaseHajj3Step1: After Fajr prayer on the 8th of Dhul Hijjah — those performing Hajj Tamattu re-enter Ihram from their accommodation in Makkah
phaseHajj3Step2: Make the Niyyah for Hajj and begin reciting Talbiyah again
phaseHajj3Step3: Travel to Mina — it is approximately 8km from Masjid Al-Haram
phaseHajj3Step4: Arrive in Mina and locate your assigned tent
phaseHajj3Step5: Pray Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha in Mina — shorten prayers to 2 rakats (Qasr) but do NOT combine them in Mina
phaseHajj3Step6: Pray Fajr the next morning in Mina before departing to Arafah
phaseHajj3Step7: Spend the night in Mina in worship — dhikr, dua, Quran recitation and salawat
phaseHajj3Step8: Prepare your duas for Arafah — write them down, organise them. Tomorrow is the most important day
phaseHajj3Step9: Sleep early if you can — the Day of Arafah requires full energy and presence
phaseHajj3Tip1: Mina is a city of tents — your tent is assigned by your Hajj group. Do not wander too far and memorise landmarks near your tent
phaseHajj3Tip2: The distance from the Haram to Mina is about 8km — many pilgrims walk. Your Hajj group will arrange transport
phaseHajj3Tip3: Prayers in Mina are shortened (Qasr) to 2 rakats but NOT combined — pray each prayer at its own time
phaseHajj3Tip4: This is the only location in Hajj where prayers are shortened but not combined — many people make the mistake of combining
phaseHajj3Tip5: Use the night in Mina wisely — make a complete list of duas for Arafah. Ask for everything — dunya and akhirah
phaseHajj3Tip6: The Prophet ﷺ spent this night in Mina in worship — follow his Sunnah
phaseHajj3Tip7: Think of Ibrahim عليه السلام — he walked through Mina on his way to sacrifice his son. You are walking in his footsteps
phaseHajj3Tip8: Keep your mobile phone charged — you will need it for navigation and communication in the crowds
phaseHajj3Tip9: Stay hydrated — the nights in Mina can still be warm and the next day will be very long
phaseHajj4Description: The 9th of Dhul Hijjah — Yawm Arafah — is the most important day in the Islamic calendar. It is the pillar of Hajj — the Prophet ﷺ said 'Hajj is Arafah'. Missing this day means missing Hajj entirely. On this day Allah descends to the lowest heaven and boasts about His servants to the angels saying 'Look at my servants — they have come dishevelled and dusty from every distant pass. They hope for My mercy.' On no other day are more people freed from the Fire than on the Day of Arafah. Every dua you make, every tear you shed, every moment of dhikr — it all counts. Do not waste a single second.
phaseHajj4Dua1Title: The best dua on the Day of Arafah — repeat constantly
phaseHajj4Dua1Translation: There is no god but Allah alone, no partner has He. His is the dominion and His is the praise and He is powerful over everything — the Prophet ﷺ said this is the best dua on the Day of Arafah
phaseHajj4Dua2Translation: O Allah You are Pardoning and Generous, You love to pardon so pardon me
phaseHajj4Dua3Title: Dua of complete submission at Arafah
phaseHajj4Dua3Translation: O Allah Yours is all praise as we say and better than what we say. O Allah to You belongs my prayer, my worship, my life and my death and to You is my return
phaseHajj4Dua4Title: Dua for yourself — pour your heart out
phaseHajj4Dua4Translation: O Allah forgive me, have mercy on me, guide me, grant me well-being and provide for me
phaseHajj4Dua5Translation: My Lord forgive me and my parents and have mercy on them as they raised me when I was young
phaseHajj4Dua6Title: Dua for the entire Ummah at Arafah
phaseHajj4Dua6Translation: O Allah reform the Ummah of Muhammad, O Allah relieve the Ummah of Muhammad, O Allah have mercy on the Ummah of Muhammad
phaseHajj4Dua7Title: Dua for Jannah and protection from Jahannam
phaseHajj4Dua7Translation: O Allah I ask You for Paradise and I seek refuge in You from the Fire
phaseHajj4Dua8Title: Bonus — dua of complete dependence on Allah
phaseHajj4Dua8Translation: O Ever-Living O Self-Sustaining, by Your mercy I seek help. Set right all my affairs and do not leave me to myself for even the blink of an eye
phaseHajj4Dua9Title: Bonus — dua for hidayah for loved ones
phaseHajj4Dua9Translation: O Allah guide my heart and the hearts of my family to the straight path
phaseHajj4FemaleNote: Women should make the absolute most of Arafah — this day is equal for men and women before Allah. There are no gender differences in the rituals of Arafah. Women stand, make dua, cry, ask and give their heart to Allah just as the men do. If a woman is in her menstrual cycle she still performs the Wuquf at Arafah — her Hajj is completely valid. Women should find a quiet corner of the tent or the plain, face the Qibla, raise their hands and pour their heart out to Allah. This is your day too.
phaseHajj4Step1: Depart from Mina to Arafah after Fajr prayer on the 9th of Dhul Hijjah
phaseHajj4Step10: Pray Maghrib and Isha combined at Muzdalifah — not at Arafah
phaseHajj4Step2: Arafah is approximately 14km from Makkah — your Hajj group will arrange transport
phaseHajj4Step3: Arrive at Arafah and locate your tent — the plain of Arafah is enormous
phaseHajj4Step4: Combine and shorten Dhuhr and Asr prayers — pray them together at Dhuhr time (2 rakats each)
phaseHajj4Step5: The Wuquf (standing) at Arafah begins after Dhuhr and lasts until sunset — this is the pillar of Hajj
phaseHajj4Step6: Face the Qibla, raise your hands and make continuous dua — do not stop
phaseHajj4Step7: Alternate between dua, dhikr, Quran recitation, salawat and istighfar throughout the afternoon
phaseHajj4Step8: Do not leave Arafah before sunset — leaving early invalidates the Hajj
phaseHajj4Step9: After sunset depart calmly to Muzdalifah — do not rush or push
phaseHajj4Tip1: This is the day — do not waste it on talking, eating, sleeping or your phone. Every second is priceless
phaseHajj4Tip10: The boundaries of Arafah are clearly marked — make sure you are within the boundaries. Jabal Ar-Rahmah (the Mount of Mercy) is inside Arafah but standing on it is not required — anywhere within the plain is valid
phaseHajj4Tip2: Write your duas before you arrive at Arafah — in the emotion of the moment you may forget what you wanted to ask
phaseHajj4Tip3: Cry if you can — tears at Arafah are a sign of a soft and present heart. If you cannot cry then try to cry
phaseHajj4Tip4: The Prophet ﷺ performed the Wuquf on his camel facing the Qibla with his hands raised — follow this Sunnah
phaseHajj4Tip5: Do not spend Arafah sleeping in the tent — be outside facing the Qibla making dua for as long as you can
phaseHajj4Tip6: Alternate between the best dua (La ilaha illallah wahdahu...) and your personal duas — this is the Sunnah
phaseHajj4Tip7: Make dua for everyone who asked you — your parents, your family, the sick, the oppressed, the entire Ummah
phaseHajj4Tip8: The Prophet ﷺ said on this day Allah frees more people from the Fire than on any other day — be one of them
phaseHajj4Tip9: Do not leave Arafah before sunset under any circumstances — this is a condition of valid Hajj
phaseHajj5Description: After the spiritual peak of Arafah you descend to Muzdalifah — an open plain between Arafah and Mina where you will spend the night under the open sky. No tents, no hotels, no comforts — just you, millions of fellow pilgrims and the stars above. This is one of the most humbling and beautiful nights of Hajj. The Prophet ﷺ prayed Maghrib and Isha combined here, collected pebbles, rested and then prayed Fajr before departing to Mina. Follow his Sunnah as closely as you can. The tiredness you feel after Arafah is real — but push through. This night is short and immensely blessed.
phaseHajj5Dua1Translation: O Allah You have said call upon Me and I will respond to you and You never break Your promise
phaseHajj5Dua2Title: Dua after Fajr at Muzdalifah facing the Qibla
phaseHajj5Dua2Translation: There is no god but Allah alone, no partner has He. His is the dominion and His is the praise and He is powerful over everything
phaseHajj5Dua3Title: Dua for the night under the sky
phaseHajj5Dua3Translation: O Allah place light in my heart, light in my hearing and light in my sight
phaseHajj5Dua4Title: Bonus — dua of gratitude after Arafah
phaseHajj5Dua4Translation: All praise be to Allah who guided us to this — we would never have been guided had Allah not guided us
phaseHajj5Dua5Title: Bonus — dua for protection through the night
phaseHajj5Dua5Translation: In Your name O Allah I live and in Your name I die
phaseHajj5Dua6Title: Bonus — dua before sleeping at Muzdalifah
phaseHajj5Dua6Translation: O Allah protect me from Your punishment on the day You resurrect Your servants
phaseHajj5FemaleNote: Women and those with children or the elderly in their care are explicitly permitted by the Prophet ﷺ to leave Muzdalifah after midnight — you do not need to wait for Fajr. This is not a concession out of weakness — it is a mercy from Allah and a ruling from the Prophet ﷺ himself. Women who leave early should still collect their pebbles before departing. Arriving at Mina early allows women to stone the Jamarat before the crowds build up — this is actually better and safer for women.
phaseHajj5Step1: Depart from Arafah after sunset — move calmly and do not rush or push
phaseHajj5Step10: Depart to Mina after Fajr — the weak, elderly and women may depart after midnight
phaseHajj5Step2: Recite Talbiyah and dhikr throughout the journey to Muzdalifah
phaseHajj5Step3: Upon arriving at Muzdalifah pray Maghrib and Isha combined and shortened — Maghrib 3 rakats, Isha 2 rakats
phaseHajj5Step4: Collect 49 pebbles if leaving after midnight or 70 pebbles if staying until Fajr — each pebble should be the size of a chickpea
phaseHajj5Step5: Pebbles can be collected anywhere in Muzdalifah — you do not need to search for a specific spot
phaseHajj5Step6: Rest and sleep — your body needs recovery after Arafah and before the demanding Day of Eid
phaseHajj5Step7: Wake for Tahajjud if you are able — the night of Muzdalifah is precious
phaseHajj5Step8: Pray Fajr at Muzdalifah — this is Sunnah
phaseHajj5Step9: After Fajr face the Qibla and make abundant dua until it becomes light
phaseHajj5Tip1: Muzdalifah has no tents or shelter — you sleep on the ground under the open sky. Bring a light blanket or sleeping bag
phaseHajj5Tip2: The night is short — Arafah ends at sunset and Fajr comes early. Sleep quickly and wake for Fajr
phaseHajj5Tip3: Collect pebbles carefully — they should be the size of a chickpea, not too large. Washing them is not required
phaseHajj5Tip4: You need 49 pebbles if leaving early or 70 if staying for all 3 days of Tashreeq — collect extra just in case
phaseHajj5Tip5: The Prophet ﷺ made abundant dua after Fajr at Muzdalifah facing the Qibla until it became quite light — do the same
phaseHajj5Tip6: The elderly, sick and women with children are permitted to leave after midnight — this is a valid concession
phaseHajj5Tip7: Muzdalifah is a Mash'ar — a sacred marker. The Quran mentions it — 'When you depart from Arafah remember Allah at Al-Mash'ar Al-Haram'
phaseHajj5Tip8: Despite the tiredness push yourself to make dua after Fajr — this is one of the most accepted times for dua in all of Hajj
phaseHajj5Tip9: Keep your pebbles in a small bag or pouch — you will need them organised for the stoning of the Jamarat
phaseHajj6Description: The 10th of Dhul Hijjah — Yawm Al-Nahr — Eid Al-Adha. This is the busiest and most demanding day of Hajj. Four major rituals must be performed — stoning the large Jamarat, offering the sacrifice, shaving or trimming the hair and performing Tawaf Al-Ifadah. They should be done in this order following the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ. This is also the day the Talbiyah stops — you have been answering the call of Allah since Ihram and now you arrive at the moment of completion. The stoning of the Jamarat commemorates Ibrahim عليه السلام stoning Shaytan when he tried to dissuade him from sacrificing his son. With every pebble you throw you are declaring — I choose Allah over everything.
phaseHajj6Dua1Title: When throwing each pebble at the Jamarat
phaseHajj6Dua1Translation: Allah is the Greatest — say this with every single pebble thrown
phaseHajj6Dua2Translation: O Allah make it an accepted Hajj, a forgiven sin and an appreciated effort
phaseHajj6Dua3Title: Dua when shaving or cutting hair
phaseHajj6Dua3Translation: O Allah forgive those who shave, O Allah forgive those who shave, O Allah forgive those who shave and those who trim — the Prophet ﷺ made dua 3 times for those who shave
phaseHajj6Dua4Title: Dua at the start of Tawaf Al-Ifadah
phaseHajj6Dua4Translation: In the name of Allah, Allah is the Greatest. O Allah out of faith in You, belief in Your Book, fulfillment of Your covenant and following the Sunnah of Your Prophet
phaseHajj6Dua5Title: Bonus — dua of Ibrahim عليه السلام at the moment of sacrifice
phaseHajj6Dua5Translation: I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth as a true believer and I am not of those who associate partners with Allah
phaseHajj6Dua6Title: Bonus — dua of gratitude on Eid day
phaseHajj6Dua6Translation: Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, there is no god but Allah, Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest and to Allah belongs all praise — the Takbeer of Eid
phaseHajj6FemaleNote: Women do NOT shave the head — cut only a fingertip length from the ends of hair. This is a firm ruling not a suggestion. Women should go to the Jamarat early — ideally after midnight from Muzdalifah before the crowds peak. Women should stay close to their Mahram at the Jamarat — the crowds can be dangerous. Women perform Tawaf Al-Ifadah the same as men — 7 rounds at a normal pace without Idtiba or Raml. After Tawaf Al-Ifadah all restrictions are lifted for women as well.
phaseHajj6Step1: Arrive at the Jamarat bridge from Muzdalifah — go early to avoid the worst of the crowds
phaseHajj6Step10: Travel to Masjid Al-Haram and perform Tawaf Al-Ifadah — 7 rounds around the Kaaba
phaseHajj6Step11: Perform Sa'i if you did not do it during Tawaf Al-Qudum
phaseHajj6Step12: After Tawaf Al-Ifadah all Ihram restrictions are fully lifted including marital relations
phaseHajj6Step13: Return to Mina for the nights of Tashreeq
phaseHajj6Step2: Stop reciting the Talbiyah when you begin the stoning
phaseHajj6Step3: Stone only the large Jamarat (Jamarat Al-Aqabah) today — throw 7 pebbles one at a time
phaseHajj6Step4: Say Allahu Akbar with each throw — throw with purpose and intention not just mechanically
phaseHajj6Step5: The pebble must land in the basin — if it misses throw another
phaseHajj6Step6: After stoning arrange for the sacrifice (Hady) — your Hajj group will handle this or you can use an authorised online service
phaseHajj6Step7: After the sacrifice — men shave the entire head (Halq) which is more rewarding or trim from all parts (Taqsir)
phaseHajj6Step8: Women cut only a fingertip length from the ends of hair — do not shave
phaseHajj6Step9: At this point partial Ihram ends — you may wear normal clothes and use perfume. Marital relations remain prohibited until Tawaf Al-Ifadah
phaseHajj6Tip1: Go to the Jamarat as early as possible — after midnight from Muzdalifah if you can. The crowds are smaller and it is cooler
phaseHajj6Tip10: Call your family on Eid — tell them you made dua for them at Arafah and on Eid day
phaseHajj6Tip2: The Jamarat bridge has multiple levels — use the upper levels to avoid the densest crowds on the ground floor
phaseHajj6Tip3: Throw with purpose — each pebble represents your rejection of Shaytan and your complete submission to Allah
phaseHajj6Tip4: The order matters — stone first, then sacrifice, then shave, then Tawaf. Doing them out of order requires expiation
phaseHajj6Tip5: Tawaf Al-Ifadah is obligatory — Hajj is not complete without it. Do not delay it beyond the 12th of Dhul Hijjah
phaseHajj6Tip6: After Tawaf Al-Ifadah drink Zamzam water abundantly — you are now fully out of Ihram
phaseHajj6Tip7: The sacrifice does not have to be done by your own hands — authorised services allow you to arrange it and it counts
phaseHajj6Tip8: Eid in Mina is unlike any Eid anywhere else on earth — millions of people in white all celebrating together
phaseHajj6Tip9: Despite the exhaustion — this day is one you will remember for the rest of your life. Be fully present
phaseHajj7Description: The 11th, 12th and 13th of Dhul Hijjah are called Ayyam Al-Tashreeq — the Days of Drying Meat — named after the practice of drying sacrificial meat in the sun. These are days of celebration, gratitude and continued worship. You remain in Mina and stone all three Jamarat each day. Allah mentions these days in the Quran — 'And remember Allah during the appointed days.' The Prophet ﷺ said these are days of eating, drinking and remembrance of Allah. Do not let the physical exhaustion of the previous days stop you from filling these days with dhikr, dua and gratitude. You are still in one of the holiest places on earth — make every moment count.
phaseHajj7Dua1Title: When throwing each pebble — all three Jamarat
phaseHajj7Dua1Translation: Allah is the Greatest — say with every single pebble
phaseHajj7Dua2Title: Dua after stoning the small Jamarat — face Qibla and raise hands
phaseHajj7Dua2Translation: O Allah make it an accepted Hajj, an appreciated effort, a forgiven sin and a righteous deed that is accepted
phaseHajj7Dua3Title: Dua after stoning the medium Jamarat — face Qibla and raise hands
phaseHajj7Dua3Translation: O Allah I seek refuge in You from the accursed Shaytan and from every rebellious devil
phaseHajj7Dua4Title: Takbeer of Tashreeq — recite after every fard prayer these days
phaseHajj7Dua4Translation: Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, there is no god but Allah, Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest and to Allah belongs all praise
phaseHajj7Dua5Title: Dua for the remaining days of Tashreeq
phaseHajj7Dua5Translation: Our Lord give us good in this world and good in the hereafter and save us from the punishment of the Fire
phaseHajj7Dua6Title: Bonus — dua of gratitude for completing Hajj rituals
phaseHajj7Dua6Translation: All praise be to Allah by whose grace all good deeds are completed
phaseHajj7Dua7Title: Bonus — dua in Mina during the blessed days
phaseHajj7Dua7Translation: Glory be to Allah and His is the praise, glory be to Allah the Most Great — the Prophet ﷺ said these two phrases are beloved to Allah, light on the tongue and heavy on the scales
phaseHajj7Dua8Title: Bonus — dua for acceptance before leaving Mina
phaseHajj7Dua8Translation: O Allah accept from us, indeed You are the All-Hearing the All-Knowing, and turn to us in forgiveness, indeed You are the Ever-Relenting the Most Merciful
phaseHajj7FemaleNote: Women should go to the Jamarat with their Mahram and ideally at less crowded times — early afternoon just after Dhuhr or later in the evening. Women are permitted to delay the stoning to nighttime if the crowds are too dangerous during the day — this is a valid concession for safety. Women recite the Takbeer of Tashreeq after every fard prayer quietly. Women who left Muzdalifah early on Eid night already stoned the large Jamarat — they begin the days of Tashreeq stoning all three Jamarat from the 11th.
phaseHajj7Step1: Spend the nights of the 11th, 12th and 13th in Mina — spending the night in Mina is obligatory
phaseHajj7Step10: Those who do not leave before sunset on the 12th must stay and stone on the 13th as well
phaseHajj7Step11: After the final stoning on the last day depart to Makkah for Tawaf Al-Wadaa
phaseHajj7Step2: Each day after Dhuhr time — stone all three Jamarat in order: small (Jamarat Al-Sughra), medium (Jamarat Al-Wusta) then large (Jamarat Al-Aqabah)
phaseHajj7Step3: Throw 7 pebbles at each Jamarat — 21 pebbles per day, 49 total if leaving on the 12th or 70 total if staying until the 13th
phaseHajj7Step4: Say Allahu Akbar with each throw
phaseHajj7Step5: After stoning the small Jamarat — move to the side, face the Qibla and make a long dua
phaseHajj7Step6: After stoning the medium Jamarat — move to the side, face the Qibla and make a long dua
phaseHajj7Step7: After stoning the large Jamarat — do not stop for dua here, move on
phaseHajj7Step8: Stoning must be done after Dhuhr time — stoning before Dhuhr on these days is not valid
phaseHajj7Step9: Those wishing to leave early may depart on the 12th before sunset — this is called the Rukhsa (concession)
phaseHajj7Tip1: Stone after Dhuhr time each day — this is a condition for validity. Stoning before Dhuhr on the days of Tashreeq is not accepted according to the majority of scholars
phaseHajj7Tip10: The crowds at the Jamarat thin out significantly after the first day — the 12th and 13th are much easier
phaseHajj7Tip2: The order of the three Jamarat matters — small first, then medium, then large. Do not change the order
phaseHajj7Tip3: After the small and medium Jamarat move to the side face the Qibla and make a long dua — this is the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ
phaseHajj7Tip4: Do not stop for dua after the large Jamarat — move on. This is also the Sunnah
phaseHajj7Tip5: If you wish to leave on the 12th — depart before sunset. If the sun sets while you are still in Mina you must stay and stone on the 13th
phaseHajj7Tip6: Staying until the 13th and stoning all three days is more complete and more rewarding — the Prophet ﷺ stayed
phaseHajj7Tip7: These days are days of eating and drinking — it is prohibited to fast on the days of Tashreeq
phaseHajj7Tip8: Recite the Takbeer of Tashreeq after every fard prayer from Fajr of the 9th until Asr of the 13th
phaseHajj7Tip9: Use the time between stonings for dhikr, Quran, dua and rest — do not waste these precious days
phaseHajj8Description: Tawaf Al-Wadaa — the Farewell Tawaf — is the last act of Hajj and one of the most emotionally overwhelming moments of the entire journey. You are about to say goodbye to the Kaaba — and nobody knows if they will ever return. The Prophet ﷺ instructed that no one should leave Makkah without making this their final act. As you circle the Kaaba for the last time let every round carry the weight of gratitude — for being chosen, for being guided, for being forgiven. Many pilgrims weep uncontrollably during the farewell Tawaf. Let your tears fall freely — they are from Allah and they return to Allah.
phaseHajj8Dua1Title: Dua at the Multazam — press against the wall and pour your heart out
phaseHajj8Dua1Translation: O Allah this house is Your house and the servant is Your servant, the son of Your servant and the son of Your maidservant. You carried me on what You subjected for me of Your creation and transported me through Your lands until You brought me by Your grace to Your house
phaseHajj8Dua2Title: Dua for return to the Haram — the most important farewell dua
phaseHajj8Dua2Translation: O Allah do not make this our last visit to Your Sacred House and make it easy for us to return to it
phaseHajj8Dua3Title: Dua when leaving the Haram for the last time
phaseHajj8Dua3Translation: O Allah I ask You to grant me a return to Your Sacred House in health and ease
phaseHajj8Dua4Title: Dua of gratitude for completing Hajj
phaseHajj8Dua4Translation: Our Lord accept from us, indeed You are the All-Hearing the All-Knowing, and turn to us in forgiveness, indeed You are the Ever-Relenting the Most Merciful
phaseHajj8Dua5Title: Dua for the whole Ummah before leaving
phaseHajj8Dua5Translation: O Allah reform the Ummah of Muhammad, O Allah relieve the Ummah of Muhammad, O Allah have mercy on the Ummah of Muhammad
phaseHajj8Dua6Title: Bonus — dua under the Mizab (golden waterspout of the Kaaba)
phaseHajj8Dua6Translation: O Allah shade me under the shade of Your Throne on the day when there is no shade except Your shade
phaseHajj8Dua7Title: Bonus — final salawat upon the Prophet ﷺ before leaving
phaseHajj8Dua7Translation: O Allah send blessings and peace upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad as You sent blessings and peace upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim. Indeed You are Praiseworthy and Glorious
phaseHajj8FemaleNote: Women in their menstrual cycle are completely excused from Tawaf Al-Wadaa — there is no penalty and no expiation required. This is an explicit concession from the Prophet ﷺ himself. Women who are pure perform Tawaf Al-Wadaa exactly like any other Tawaf — 7 rounds at a normal pace. Women should try to reach the Multazam if possible — go during a quieter time. If it is too crowded face it from wherever you are and raise your hands. The farewell is the same for men and women — heavy hearts, grateful tears and the hope of return.
phaseHajj8Step1: After completing the stoning on your final day in Mina — collect your belongings and travel to Makkah
phaseHajj8Step10: Do not stay in Makkah long after the farewell Tawaf — depart as soon as reasonably possible
phaseHajj8Step2: Go directly to Masjid Al-Haram for Tawaf Al-Wadaa — this should be your last act before leaving Makkah
phaseHajj8Step3: Perform 7 rounds of Tawaf around the Kaaba — the same as any other Tawaf
phaseHajj8Step4: Pray 2 rakats behind Maqam Ibrahim after completing the 7 rounds
phaseHajj8Step5: Drink Zamzam water — make dua while drinking. This may be the last Zamzam you drink for a long time
phaseHajj8Step6: Go to the Multazam — the area between the Black Stone and the door of the Kaaba — press your chest and face against it and make dua. This is one of the most powerful spots for dua in the entire world
phaseHajj8Step7: Make dua at Maqam Ibrahim, under the Mizab (the golden waterspout) and in the Hijr Ismail if possible
phaseHajj8Step8: Take one last look at the Kaaba — let it fill your heart and your memory
phaseHajj8Step9: Leave the Haram walking backwards if you can — keeping your face towards the Kaaba as long as possible
phaseHajj8Tip1: The Multazam is between the Black Stone and the door of the Kaaba — press your chest, face, hands and forearms against the wall and make dua. This is one of the most powerful spots for dua on earth
phaseHajj8Tip10: The journey home begins — but Hajj has changed you forever. Now live like it
phaseHajj8Tip2: If you cannot reach the Multazam due to crowds — face it from wherever you are and raise your hands. The intention is what matters
phaseHajj8Tip3: The Hijr Ismail — the semi-circular area adjacent to the Kaaba — is actually part of the Kaaba. Praying inside it counts as praying inside the Kaaba. Try to pray 2 rakats inside it if possible
phaseHajj8Tip4: Tawaf Al-Wadaa is obligatory for all pilgrims except women in their menstrual cycle — they are excused without any expiation required
phaseHajj8Tip5: Do not stay in Makkah for unnecessary shopping or activities after the farewell Tawaf — depart promptly
phaseHajj8Tip6: Many pilgrims cry during the farewell Tawaf — do not hold back. These tears are precious
phaseHajj8Tip7: Take photos of the Kaaba to keep — but do not let the camera replace the experience. Be present
phaseHajj8Tip8: The last thing your eyes should see of Makkah is the Kaaba — look back as long as you can
phaseHajj8Tip9: Ask Allah sincerely to bring you back — those who ask with a sincere heart are often answered
phaseHajj9Description: Alhamdulillah. You have completed Hajj — the fifth pillar of Islam and the greatest physical act of worship a Muslim can perform in their lifetime. You stood at Arafah. You spent the night at Muzdalifah under the open sky. You stoned the Jamarat. You performed Tawaf Al-Ifadah and said farewell to the Kaaba. The Prophet ﷺ said the reward of a Mabrur Hajj is nothing but Jannah. There is no greater transaction in the history of humanity — you gave Allah a few days of your life and He gives you eternal paradise in return. Now comes the hardest part — going home and living like a person who has been to the House of Allah. The real Hajj begins when you return.
phaseHajj9Dua1Title: Dua of complete acceptance — say this from your heart
phaseHajj9Dua1Translation: Our Lord accept from us, indeed You are the All-Hearing the All-Knowing
phaseHajj9Dua2Title: Dua of gratitude for being chosen
phaseHajj9Dua2Translation: O Allah all praise belongs to You, all gratitude belongs to You, all good is in Your hands and all matters return to You
phaseHajj9Dua3Translation: O Allah make me of those who when given they are grateful, when tested they are patient and when they sin they seek forgiveness
phaseHajj9Dua4Translation: O Allah make it an accepted Hajj, an appreciated effort, a forgiven sin and a trade that will never perish
phaseHajj9Dua5Title: Dua for return to the Haram
phaseHajj9Dua5Translation: O Allah do not make this our last visit to Your Sacred House and grant us a return to it in good health
phaseHajj9Dua6Title: Dua for the entire Ummah upon returning home
phaseHajj9Dua6Translation: O Allah reform the Ummah of Muhammad, O Allah relieve the Ummah of Muhammad, O Allah have mercy on the Ummah of Muhammad
phaseHajj9Dua7Title: Bonus — dua when entering your home after Hajj
phaseHajj9Dua7Translation: O Allah I ask You for the best entering and the best exiting. In the name of Allah we enter and in the name of Allah we exit and upon Allah our Lord we rely
phaseHajj9Dua8Title: Bonus — dua for parents after returning from Hajj
phaseHajj9Dua8Translation: My Lord forgive me and my parents, have mercy on them as they raised me when I was young and admit them to Paradise with the righteous
phaseHajj9Dua9Title: Bonus — the dua the Prophet ﷺ made when returning from any journey
phaseHajj9Dua9Translation: We are returning, repenting, worshipping and praising our Lord — the Prophet ﷺ said this repeatedly when returning from Hajj
phaseHajj9FemaleNote: Women who completed Hajj have achieved one of the greatest acts of worship available to any human being. The Prophet ﷺ told Aisha رضي الله عنها that Hajj is the jihad of women — and the reward of jihad in the way of Allah is Jannah. A woman who returns from Hajj carries the same purity, the same forgiveness and the same new beginning as any man. Guard it. Women should share their Hajj experience with other women in their community — your story may be the reason another woman makes the journey. Be the inspiration.
phaseHajj9Step1: Reflect in silence — sit wherever you are and let the reality of what you just completed wash over you
phaseHajj9Step10: Begin planning your next Umrah or return to the Haram — never let this be the last time
phaseHajj9Step2: Make a long dua of gratitude — thank Allah for your health, your means, your guidance and your acceptance
phaseHajj9Step3: Pray 2 rakats of shukr — two units of gratitude prayer for the completion of this great act of worship
phaseHajj9Step4: Call your family and loved ones — tell them you made dua for them at Arafah, at the Jamarat and at the Kaaba
phaseHajj9Step5: Make a list of 5 things you will change in your life after Hajj — write them down before you board your flight home
phaseHajj9Step6: Maintain the good habits built during Hajj — the early Fajr, the dhikr, the connection with the Quran
phaseHajj9Step7: Be patient on the journey home — the flights, the crowds, the delays. Every hardship is still expiation
phaseHajj9Step8: When you return home pray 2 rakats of shukr in your local masjid
phaseHajj9Step9: Share the experience with your community — inspire others to make the journey
phaseHajj9Tip1: The sign of a Mabrur Hajj is that you return better than you left — guard this transformation fiercely
phaseHajj9Tip10: Make dua for everyone who supported your journey — your family, your employer, your Hajj group. Gratitude to people is gratitude to Allah
phaseHajj9Tip11: A person who returns from Hajj is like a newborn — pure, forgiven and given a new beginning. What you do with that beginning is your choice
phaseHajj9Tip2: The first test of your Hajj comes the moment you land at the airport — be patient, be kind, be the person Hajj made you
phaseHajj9Tip3: Shaytan works hardest on those who have just completed great acts of worship — be vigilant
phaseHajj9Tip4: Do not go back to sins — the Prophet ﷺ compared returning to sin after sincere repentance to a dog returning to its vomit
phaseHajj9Tip5: Maintain your Fajr — if Hajj gave you anything let it be the Fajr prayer
phaseHajj9Tip6: Maintain your connection with the Quran — even 5 minutes a day is better than nothing
phaseHajj9Tip7: Give sadaqah when you return — share the barakah of Hajj with those who could not go
phaseHajj9Tip8: The Prophet ﷺ said follow up Hajj with Umrah and follow up Umrah with Hajj — start planning your return
phaseHajj9Tip9: Tell your story to inspire others — there are Muslims who have never considered Hajj because nobody told them how life-changing it is
phaseUmrah1Description: Most pilgrims begin their blessed journey in Madinah Al-Munawwarah — the illuminated city. This is the city of the Prophet ﷺ and every step here carries immense reward. Arrive with a heart full of love for the Prophet ﷺ and take full advantage of every moment in this sacred city before proceeding to Makkah.
phaseUmrah1Dua1Translation: O Allah, open for me the gates of Your mercy
phaseUmrah1Dua2Title: Salawat upon the Prophet ﷺ at his grave
phaseUmrah1Dua2Translation: O Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim. Indeed You are Praiseworthy and Glorious
phaseUmrah1Dua3Translation: Peace be upon you O Messenger of Allah and the mercy and blessings of Allah
phaseUmrah1Dua4Translation: Glory be to Allah, all praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, and Allah is the Greatest
phaseUmrah1Dua5Title: Dua when visiting graves (Jannat Al Baqi)
phaseUmrah1Dua5Translation: Peace be upon you O people of the graves from the believers and Muslims. May Allah have mercy on those who have gone before us and those who will come after. And we will indeed, if Allah wills, join you
phaseUmrah1FemaleNote: Women should cover fully when visiting the grave area. Many scholars recommend the face covering near the grave out of respect. Women visit Jannat Al Baqi at designated times — check with the masjid staff for the current schedule. Women are not permitted inside Riyad Al Jannah during men's prayer times — go during women's designated hours.
phaseUmrah1Step1: Arrive in Madinah with the intention of visiting Masjid An-Nabawi and sending salawat upon the Prophet ﷺ
phaseUmrah1Step10: Spend time in dua, Quran recitation and salawat throughout your stay
phaseUmrah1Step2: Enter Masjid An-Nabawi with your right foot — one prayer here equals 1000 prayers anywhere else
phaseUmrah1Step3: Visit Riyad Al Jannah — the Garden of Paradise — between the Prophet's grave and his pulpit. This is a piece of Jannah on earth
phaseUmrah1Step4: Stand at the grave of the Prophet ﷺ and send salawat — face the grave not the Qibla
phaseUmrah1Step5: Move to the right to greet Abu Bakr As-Siddiq رضي الله عنه, then further right to greet Umar Ibn Al-Khattab رضي الله عنه
phaseUmrah1Step6: Visit Jannat Al Baqi — the graveyard of the companions — and make dua for them
phaseUmrah1Step7: Visit Masjid Quba — the first masjid built in Islam. Praying 2 rakats here equals the reward of a complete Umrah
phaseUmrah1Step8: Visit Masjid Al-Qiblatayn — the masjid of the two Qiblas where the direction of prayer was changed
phaseUmrah1Step9: Visit the sites of the Battle of Uhud and the grave of Hamza رضي الله عنه the uncle of the Prophet ﷺ
phaseUmrah1Tip1: Visit Riyad Al Jannah very early — before Fajr or right after — to avoid the enormous crowds
phaseUmrah1Tip2: You may only enter Riyad Al Jannah through specific doors — ask the guards which entrance is open
phaseUmrah1Tip3: Spend at least 2-3 days in Madinah to benefit fully from its blessings
phaseUmrah1Tip4: The Prophet ﷺ said whoever visits him after his death it is as if they visited him during his life
phaseUmrah1Tip5: Make a list of duas before you visit — standing at the grave of the Prophet ﷺ is a powerful moment
phaseUmrah1Tip6: The 40 prayers (Arba'een) — praying 40 consecutive prayers in Masjid An-Nabawi — is highly recommended
phaseUmrah1Tip7: Buy dates from Madinah — the Ajwa date is especially recommended by the Prophet ﷺ
phaseUmrah2Description: Ihram is the sacred state you must enter before performing Umrah. It is both a physical and spiritual transformation — you strip away all worldly distinctions and stand equal before Allah. Rich and poor, king and servant, all wear the same simple white garments. The Miqat is the designated boundary — you must enter Ihram before crossing it. Crossing without Ihram requires a penalty (dam).
phaseUmrah2Dua1Translation: Here I am O Allah, for Umrah
phaseUmrah2Dua2Translation: Here I am O Allah, here I am. Here I am, You have no partner, here I am. Verily all praise, grace and sovereignty belong to You. You have no partner.
phaseUmrah2Dua3Translation: O Allah I intend to perform Umrah so make it easy for me and accept it from me
phaseUmrah2Dua4Translation: O Allah I seek refuge in You from disbelief, poverty and the punishment of the grave
phaseUmrah2FemaleNote: Women wear their normal modest clothing in any colour — no special garment is required. Women do NOT cover the face or hands during Ihram — this is prohibited during Ihram according to the majority of scholars. Women recite the Talbiyah quietly so only they can hear. Women in their menstrual cycle still perform Ghusl and enter Ihram — they simply delay Tawaf until they are pure. Do not delay your trip because of your cycle.
phaseUmrah2Step1: Trim nails and remove unwanted body hair before Ghusl — you cannot do this after entering Ihram
phaseUmrah2Step2: Perform Ghusl (full body purification bath) with the intention of Ihram — this is Sunnah even for women in their menstrual cycle
phaseUmrah2Step3: Men apply perfume to the body before putting on Ihram — not to the garments themselves
phaseUmrah2Step4: Men wear the two white unstitched sheets — Izar (lower) and Rida (upper). No underwear, no stitched clothing
phaseUmrah2Step5: Women wear their normal modest clothing in any colour — there is no special Ihram garment for women
phaseUmrah2Step6: Pray 2 rakats of Ihram sunnah prayer — recite Surah Al-Kafirun in the first rakat and Surah Al-Ikhlas in the second
phaseUmrah2Step7: Make the Niyyah (intention) for Umrah at the Miqat — say it aloud
phaseUmrah2Step8: Begin reciting the Talbiyah — men loudly, women quietly
phaseUmrah2Step8Translit: Labbayk Allahumma Labbayk, Labbayka la sharika laka labbayk, Innal-hamda wan-ni'mata laka wal-mulk, La sharika lak.
phaseUmrah2Step9: From this moment all Ihram restrictions apply — avoid them carefully until you complete your Umrah
phaseUmrah2Tip1: The main Miqats for Umrah are: Dhul Hulayfah (for those coming from Madinah), Juhfah (Syria/Egypt), Qarn Al-Manazil (Najd), Yalamlam (Yemen), Dhat Irq (Iraq)
phaseUmrah2Tip2: If flying directly to Jeddah — you must put on Ihram on the plane before reaching the Miqat boundary. The captain will announce it
phaseUmrah2Tip3: Once in Ihram you may NOT: cut hair or nails, use perfume, cover the head (men), wear stitched clothing (men), engage in marital relations, hunt animals, or cause harm to others
phaseUmrah2Tip4: If you accidentally violate any restriction — make istighfar immediately and consult a scholar about whether a penalty applies
phaseUmrah2Tip5: Keep reciting Talbiyah throughout your journey until you begin Tawaf — at every moment, especially when going uphill, downhill, boarding transport or meeting other pilgrims
phaseUmrah2Tip6: Ihram is not just physical — it is a state of the heart. Avoid arguments, bad speech and anything that angers Allah
phaseUmrah2Tip7: The Prophet ﷺ said: whoever performs Hajj or Umrah without committing any obscenity or sin returns free from sins, like the day his mother gave birth to him.
phaseUmrah3Description: Arriving in Makkah Al-Mukarramah — the Most Noble City — is one of the most overwhelming spiritual experiences a Muslim can have. Your heart will race as you approach Masjid Al-Haram. The moment you first see the Kaaba is one of the most powerful moments of your entire life — duas made at that moment are accepted. Prepare your heart and have your duas ready before you enter.
phaseUmrah3Dua1Translation: O Allah this is Your sanctuary and Your place of safety, so forbid my flesh to the Hellfire, keep me safe from Your punishment on the day You resurrect Your servants, and make me among Your close friends and those who obey You
phaseUmrah3Dua2Translation: In the name of Allah, and peace and blessings upon the Messenger of Allah. O Allah forgive my sins and open for me the gates of Your mercy
phaseUmrah3Dua3Title: Dua upon first seeing the Kaaba — raise your hands and ask
phaseUmrah3Dua3Translation: O Allah You are Peace and from You comes peace, so greet us our Lord with peace
phaseUmrah3Dua4Title: Bonus dua upon seeing the Kaaba — ask for anything
phaseUmrah3Dua4Translation: O Allah increase this House in honour, greatness, nobility and reverence, and increase those who honour and respect it — those who perform Hajj or Umrah — in honour, nobility, greatness and righteousness
phaseUmrah3Dua5Translation: O Allah I ask You for beneficial knowledge, abundant provision and cure from every disease
phaseUmrah3FemaleNote: Women should enter the Haram modestly and move carefully through crowds — hold onto a mahram if possible. Women do not need to rush or push to reach the Black Stone — pointing from a distance is completely valid and accepted. Avoid coming very close to the Kaaba during peak times for your own safety. The upper floors of the Haram are often less crowded and the view of the Kaaba from above is breathtaking.
phaseUmrah3Step1: Enter Makkah reciting the dua for entering a city — be in a state of wudu if possible
phaseUmrah3Step2: Head directly to Masjid Al-Haram — enter with your right foot reciting the masjid entry dua
phaseUmrah3Step2Translation: O Allah, open for me the gates of Your mercy
phaseUmrah3Step3: Walk towards the Kaaba slowly and with full presence of heart — do not rush
phaseUmrah3Step4: As you approach the courtyard, keep your gaze lowered.
phaseUmrah3Step5: When the Kaaba first comes into view, look up, stop, raise your hands, and make abundant dua.
phaseUmrah3Step6: Stop reciting the Talbiyah out loud as you approach the boundary and prepare to begin your Tawaf.
phaseUmrah3Step7: Proceed to the Black Stone (Hajr Al-Aswad) to begin your Tawaf
phaseUmrah3Step8: If you cannot reach the Black Stone due to heavy crowds, point to it from a distance and say Allahu Akbar.
phaseUmrah3Step8ModalText: Face the Black Stone line, raise your right hand straight out with your palm facing the Kaaba, and say "Allahu Akbar" to begin your lap.
phaseUmrah3Tip1: Have a list of duas written or saved on your phone before you enter — the moment you see the Kaaba you may forget everything
phaseUmrah3Tip2: When you first see the Kaaba — stop, raise your hands and make abundant dua. Do not waste this sacred moment on photos
phaseUmrah3Tip3: Enter the Haram with complete humility and awe — you are standing in the most sacred place on earth
phaseUmrah3Tip4: Drink Zamzam water before starting Tawaf — the Prophet ﷺ said 'The water of Zamzam is for whatever it is drunk for.' Make your intention and dua while drinking it.
phaseUmrah3Tip4Translit: Allahumma inni as'aluka ilman nafi'an wa rizqan wasi'an wa shifa'an min kulli da'
phaseUmrah3Tip4Translation: O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, abundant provision and cure from every disease
phaseUmrah3Tip5: The Zamzam well has been flowing for over 4000 years since Allah sent it for Hajar and Ismail عليهما السلام
phaseUmrah3Tip6: If it is very crowded when you arrive — you may rest first and perform Tawaf at a quieter time such as after Tahajjud
phaseUmrah3Tip7: The best time to do Tawaf is after midnight — the crowds are smaller and the atmosphere is extraordinary
phaseUmrah3Tip8: Do not be overwhelmed by the crowds — focus only on Allah and your own worship
phaseUmrah4Description: The Kaaba is the spiritual centre of the earth and every Tawaf you do is recorded as an act of immense worship. There is no specific, mandatory dua required for each round — your heart is your guide. Speak to Allah in any language, cry, ask, thank — He hears everything.
phaseUmrah4Dua1Title: Starting each round at the Black Stone
phaseUmrah4Dua1Translation: In the name of Allah, Allah is the Greatest
phaseUmrah4Dua2Title: Between the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone — recite every round
phaseUmrah4Dua2Translation: Our Lord give us good in this world and good in the hereafter and save us from the punishment of the Fire
phaseUmrah4Dua3Title: Dua at Maqam Ibrahim after Tawaf
phaseUmrah4Dua3Translation: And take the station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer — recite this before praying 2 rakats
phaseUmrah4Dua4Translation: O Allah I ask You for beneficial knowledge, abundant provision and cure from every disease
phaseUmrah4Dua5Title: Bonus — dua for forgiveness during Tawaf
phaseUmrah4Dua5Translation: Glory be to Allah, all praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, Allah is the Greatest, and there is no power or strength except with Allah
phaseUmrah4Dua6Title: Bonus — dua to repeat throughout Tawaf
phaseUmrah4Dua6Translation: My Lord forgive and have mercy, for You are the Most Mighty the Most Generous
phaseUmrah4FemaleNote: Women do NOT perform Idtiba (exposing the shoulder) or Raml (brisk walking) — walk at a normal comfortable pace for all 7 rounds. Women should avoid the innermost circles around the Kaaba during peak times for safety — the outer circles are equally valid. If a woman is unable to touch or reach the Black Stone she simply points from wherever she is — this is completely acceptable. Women may perform Tawaf during their menstrual cycle according to some scholars in cases of necessity — consult a scholar before your trip if this may apply to you.
phaseUmrah4Step1: Make sure you are in a state of wudu before starting Tawaf — it is a strict requirement.
phaseUmrah4Step2: Men perform Idtiba — expose the right shoulder by placing the Rida under the right arm. Keep it exposed for all 7 rounds.
phaseUmrah4Step2Note: ⚠️ Note: You must cover your shoulder again as soon as the 7th round ends, before praying.
phaseUmrah4Step3Title: Starting Position at the Black Stone (Hajr Al-Aswad)
phaseUmrah4Step3: Align yourself with the Black Stone line. Touch and kiss it if possible, touch it with your hand and kiss your hand, or simply point to it from a distance.
phaseUmrah4Step4: At the start of your very first round, point your right hand toward the Black Stone and say 'Bismillahi Allahu Akbar'.
phaseUmrah4Step5: Keep the Kaaba on your LEFT side at ALL times — you circle anti-clockwise.
phaseUmrah4Step6: Men perform Raml — brisk walking with chest out — in the first 3 rounds only. Resume normal walking for the remaining 4 rounds.
phaseUmrah4Step7: For rounds 2 through 7, each time you pass the Black Stone line, simply point your right hand and say 'Allahu Akbar' to begin the next round.
phaseUmrah4Step8Title: The Yemeni Corner (Rukn al-Yamani) to Black Stone Dua
phaseUmrah4Step8: When walking between the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone, recite the Sunnah dua: 'Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanatan wa fil-akhirati hasanatan wa qina adhaban-nar'.
phaseUmrah4Step9: After completing all 7 rounds, cover both of your shoulders (for men) and pray 2 rakats behind Maqam Ibrahim (or anywhere in the Haram if it is crowded). Recite Al-Kafirun in the first rakat and Al-Ikhlas in the second.
phaseUmrah4Step10: Go to any Zamzam water station or tap distributed around the Haram. Drink while facing the Qibla and make abundant dua while drinking.
phaseUmrah4Step11: Return to the Black Stone line one final time and touch or point to it — this marks the official completion of your Tawaf.
phaseUmrah4Tip1: There is no specific dua for each round — make any dua from your heart in any language. Allah understands all languages
phaseUmrah4Tip2: If you lose count of your rounds always assume the lesser number to be safe
phaseUmrah4Tip3: Tawaf can be performed on the ground floor, first floor or roof — go to upper floors if the ground is too crowded
phaseUmrah4Tip4: The ground floor Tawaf closest to the Kaaba is the most rewarding but also the most crowded
phaseUmrah4Tip5: Tawaf after midnight is one of the most spiritual experiences — the crowds thin out and the atmosphere is unlike anything else
phaseUmrah4Tip6: If your wudu breaks during Tawaf — leave, renew wudu, and return to continue from where you left off
phaseUmrah4Tip7: You may stop Tawaf for a fard prayer — resume after the prayer from where you stopped
phaseUmrah4Tip8: Keep your eyes on the Kaaba as much as possible — let it fill your heart
phaseUmrah4Tip9: Above the Kaaba in the 7th heaven is Al-Bayt al-Ma'mur — 70,000 angels perform Tawaf around it daily. Your Tawaf on earth mirrors theirs in the heavens.
phaseUmrah5Description: Sa'i is the ritual of walking between the hills of Safa and Marwa 7 times, commemorating one of the most powerful acts of trust in Allah ever recorded in history. Hajar — the wife of Ibrahim عليه السلام — was left alone in the desert with her infant son Ismail عليه السلام with nothing but a small amount of food and water. When it ran out she ran between Safa and Marwa desperately searching for water or any sign of help — and Allah answered her with the miracle of Zamzam. Every step you take in Sa'i is you walking in the footsteps of a woman whose trust in Allah was unshakeable. Let that move you.
phaseUmrah5Dua1Title: Upon approaching Safa — recite this ayah first
phaseUmrah5Dua1Translation: Indeed Safa and Marwa are among the symbols of Allah. So whoever makes Hajj to the House or performs Umrah there is no blame on him for walking between them
phaseUmrah5Dua2Title: Dua facing the Kaaba at Safa and Marwa — repeat 3 times
phaseUmrah5Dua2Translation: Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest and to Allah belongs all praise. There is no god but Allah alone with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise. He gives life and causes death and He is powerful over everything
phaseUmrah5Dua3Title: Dua of Hajar — the spirit of Sa'i
phaseUmrah5Dua3Translation: O Allah help me, O Allah aid me, O Allah do not leave me to myself for even the blink of an eye
phaseUmrah5Dua4Title: Bonus — dua of complete reliance on Allah
phaseUmrah5Dua4Translation: Allah is sufficient for me and what an excellent Guardian He is. What an excellent Protector and what an excellent Helper
phaseUmrah5Dua5Title: Bonus — dua between Safa and Marwa
phaseUmrah5Dua5Translation: My Lord forgive and have mercy, indeed You are the Most Mighty the Most Generous
phaseUmrah5Dua6Title: Bonus — dua for yourself and family
phaseUmrah5Dua6Translation: O Allah forgive me, my parents and the believers on the Day when the reckoning will come to pass
phaseUmrah5FemaleNote: Women do NOT run between the green lights — walk at a normal comfortable pace for the entire Sa'i. This is a ruling not just a recommendation. Women may perform Sa'i during their menstrual cycle as Sa'i does not require wudu — only Tawaf requires purity. This is an important ruling that allows women to complete their Umrah without delay. Think deeply about Hajar during Sa'i — she was a woman who single-handedly demonstrated what complete tawakkul in Allah looks like.
phaseUmrah5Step1: Proceed to Mount Safa after completing Tawaf and drinking Zamzam water
phaseUmrah5Step10: Make abundant dua at both Safa and Marwa — these are blessed places
phaseUmrah5Step2: As you approach Safa recite the ayah — Innas-Safa wal-Marwata min sha'a'irillah
phaseUmrah5Step2Translation: Indeed Safa and Marwa are among the symbols of Allah
phaseUmrah5Step3: Climb Safa, face the Qibla (direction of the Kaaba) and raise your hands in dua
phaseUmrah5Step4: Make dua, recite dhikr and send salawat upon the Prophet ﷺ
phaseUmrah5Step5: Descend from Safa and walk towards Marwa at a normal pace
phaseUmrah5Step6: Men run between the two green lights — this commemorates Hajar's desperate running
phaseUmrah5Step7: Climb Marwa, face the Qibla and make dua — this is ONE trip (Safa to Marwa = 1)
phaseUmrah5Step8: Continue back and forth — Marwa to Safa = 2, Safa to Marwa = 3, and so on
phaseUmrah5Step9: You must complete 7 trips total — you will END at Marwa on the 7th trip
phaseUmrah5Tip1: Wudu is recommended for Sa'i but not obligatory — you may perform it without wudu if necessary
phaseUmrah5Tip2: Count your trips carefully — you start at Safa and must end at Marwa. Safa to Marwa is odd numbers (1,3,5,7) and Marwa to Safa is even numbers (2,4,6)
phaseUmrah5Tip3: Make personal dua in your own language at Safa and Marwa — Allah hears every language and knows every heart
phaseUmrah5Tip4: Think of Hajar during every trip — her trust in Allah brought forth Zamzam which still flows today. Your trust in Allah will never go unanswered
phaseUmrah5Tip5: Sa'i is performed inside the Mas'a — the enclosed walkway between Safa and Marwa. You do not go outside
phaseUmrah5Tip6: The Mas'a has multiple floors — use the upper floors if the ground floor is too crowded
phaseUmrah5Tip7: If you need to rest during Sa'i you may sit and then continue — there is no penalty for resting
phaseUmrah5Tip8: Sa'i can be performed immediately after Tawaf or delayed — but it must be completed before you exit Ihram
phaseUmrah6Description: Halq (shaving the head) or Taqsir (trimming the hair) is the final ritual of Umrah and the moment you exit the sacred state of Ihram. It is a powerful symbol of humility — you offer your hair to Allah as a sign of complete submission. The Prophet ﷺ made dua three times for those who shave and once for those who trim — so shaving is more rewarding for men. The moment your hair is cut, Umrah is complete and all Ihram restrictions are lifted.
phaseUmrah6Dua1Title: Dua when shaving or cutting hair
phaseUmrah6Dua1Translation: O Allah forgive those who shave their heads, O Allah forgive those who shave their heads, O Allah forgive those who shave their heads and those who trim their hair — this is the dua the Prophet ﷺ made 3 times for those who shave and once for those who trim
phaseUmrah6Dua2Translation: O Allah accept from us, indeed You are the All-Hearing the All-Knowing, and turn to us in forgiveness, indeed You are the Ever-Relenting the Most Merciful
phaseUmrah6Dua3Title: Bonus — dua of gratitude after Umrah
phaseUmrah6Dua3Translation: All praise be to Allah who brought us to this — we would never have been guided had Allah not guided us
phaseUmrah6Dua4Title: Bonus — dua for the entire Ummah
phaseUmrah6Dua4Translation: O Allah forgive the Muslim men and women, the believing men and women, both the living and the dead
phaseUmrah6FemaleNote: Women cut only a fingertip length — approximately 2-3 cm — from the ends of the hair. Do NOT shave the head — this is prohibited for women. You do not need to cut from every strand — gather your hair and cut a small amount from the ends. This can be done privately without exposing your hair in public. After cutting you exit Ihram and all restrictions are lifted — you may return to your normal clothing and routine.
phaseUmrah6Step1: After completing the 7th trip of Sa'i at Marwa — proceed to have your hair cut
phaseUmrah6Step2: Men — shaving the entire head (Halq) is the Sunnah and more rewarding. Trimming from all parts of the head (Taqsir) is also valid
phaseUmrah6Step3: If trimming — make sure you trim from ALL parts of the head, not just one side
phaseUmrah6Step4: Women — cut only a fingertip length (approximately 2-3 cm) from the ends of the hair. Do not shave
phaseUmrah6Step5: After cutting your hair you immediately exit Ihram — change out of the white sheets (men) into normal clothing
phaseUmrah6Step6: All Ihram restrictions are now lifted — you may use perfume, cut nails, wear normal clothes
phaseUmrah6Step7: Make dua of gratitude — your Umrah is now complete
phaseUmrah6Step8: You may now perform additional voluntary Tawaf (Tawaf An-Nafl) as many times as you wish
phaseUmrah6Tip1: The Prophet ﷺ made dua 3 times for those who shave and only once for those who trim — shaving carries far more reward for men
phaseUmrah6Tip2: You will find barbers (hallaqs) set up specifically for pilgrims right outside the Mas'a and around the Haram — they are experienced and fast
phaseUmrah6Tip3: Keep the hair you cut as a reminder of your Umrah — some pilgrims bury it
phaseUmrah6Tip4: The moment your hair is cut is one of the most emotional moments of Umrah — many people cry. Let it out
phaseUmrah6Tip5: After exiting Ihram take a shower, apply perfume and wear your best clothes — you are now returning to normal life having completed a great act of worship
phaseUmrah6Tip6: Your sins from the moment of Ihram until now have been forgiven — the Prophet ﷺ said whoever performs Umrah without committing obscenity or sin returns like the day his mother gave birth to him
phaseUmrah6Tip7: Make a list of everything you want to do differently after Umrah — this is the best time to make resolutions
phaseUmrah7Description: Alhamdulillah. You have completed your Umrah. Take a moment to sit, reflect and thank Allah for choosing you — out of billions of people on this earth, Allah invited you to His House. Not everyone who wishes to come gets to come. You were chosen. The Prophet ﷺ said that an accepted Umrah expiates all sins between it and the previous Umrah. You are leaving this place as pure as the day you were born. Now the question is — what will you do with this new beginning?
phaseUmrah7Dua1Title: Dua of acceptance — the most important dua after Umrah
phaseUmrah7Dua1Translation: Our Lord accept from us, indeed You are the All-Hearing the All-Knowing
phaseUmrah7Dua2Title: Dua of gratitude for being chosen
phaseUmrah7Dua2Translation: O Allah all praise belongs to You, all gratitude belongs to You and all matters return to You
phaseUmrah7Dua3Translation: O Allah make me of those who when they do good they rejoice and when they do wrong they seek forgiveness
phaseUmrah7Dua4Title: Dua for a return to the Haram
phaseUmrah7Dua4Translation: O Allah do not make this our last visit to Your Sacred House
phaseUmrah7Dua5Title: Tawaf Al-Wadaa — farewell dua when leaving the Haram
phaseUmrah7Dua5Translation: O Allah this house is Your house and the servant is Your servant, the son of Your servant and the son of Your maidservant. You carried me on what You have subjected for me of Your creation
phaseUmrah7Dua6Title: Bonus — dua for the whole Ummah from the Haram
phaseUmrah7Dua6Translation: O Allah reform the Ummah of Muhammad, O Allah relieve the Ummah of Muhammad, O Allah have mercy on the Ummah of Muhammad
phaseUmrah7Dua7Translation: My Lord forgive me and my parents and have mercy on them as they raised me when I was young
phaseUmrah7FemaleNote: Women should try to visit the Haram at different times — early Fajr and late night after Isha are the best times for women to access quieter areas of the Haram. Women should make the most of Tawaf An-Nafl during their remaining days — every round is immensely rewarded. Before leaving make dua at the Multazam if you can reach it — if not, raise your hands facing it from wherever you are. Ask Allah to bring you back — very few people get this opportunity and those who ask sincerely are often brought back.
phaseUmrah7Step1: Find a quiet spot in the Haram or near the Kaaba and sit in reflection — let the reality of what you just completed sink in
phaseUmrah7Step10: Before leaving Makkah perform Tawaf Al-Wadaa (farewell Tawaf) as your last act
phaseUmrah7Step2: Make a long personal dua — ask for everything. Your duas after Umrah are at their most powerful
phaseUmrah7Step3: Pray 2 rakats of shukr (gratitude) — thank Allah for the ability, health and means to perform Umrah
phaseUmrah7Step4: Perform Tawaf An-Nafl (voluntary Tawaf) as many times as you wish — every round is rewarded
phaseUmrah7Step5: Spend as much time in the Haram as possible — sitting in the Haram is worship even without doing anything
phaseUmrah7Step6: Visit the Kaaba at different times — night Tawaf after Tahajjud is one of the most beautiful experiences in existence
phaseUmrah7Step7: Drink Zamzam water abundantly — make dua with each sip
phaseUmrah7Step8: Read Quran facing the Kaaba — the reward is multiplied in the Haram
phaseUmrah7Step9: Make dua for everyone who asked you to make dua for them — you are in the best place to have duas accepted
phaseUmrah7Tip1: The sign of an accepted Umrah is that you return home a better person — guard your good deeds after you leave
phaseUmrah7Tip2: Do not go back to sins after Umrah — guard your good deeds and protect your clean slate. Every sin you return to diminishes what you worked so hard to earn.
phaseUmrah7Tip3: The best souvenir from Umrah is not dates or zamzam — it is a changed heart
phaseUmrah7Tip4: Make a list of 3 things you will change in your life after Umrah — write them down and stick to them
phaseUmrah7Tip5: Perform Tawaf An-Nafl as many times as you can during your remaining stay — every round around the Kaaba is rewarded by Allah
phaseUmrah7Tip6: Night Tawaf especially after Tahajjud is one of the most breathtaking experiences — the Haram is quieter and the atmosphere is extraordinary
phaseUmrah7Tip7: The Prophet ﷺ said — follow up Umrah with Hajj if you can. Start planning your Hajj from now
phaseUmrah7Tip8: Before leaving make dua at every blessed spot — Multazam (between the Black Stone and the Kaaba door), Maqam Ibrahim, Zamzam, Hijr Ismail
phaseUmrah7Tip9: The Multazam — the area between the Black Stone and the door of the Kaaba — is one of the most powerful spots for dua. Press your chest and face against it if you can reach it and pour your heart out

madinahPlace1Desc: Arrive in Madinah with the intention of visiting this grand mosque and sending salawat upon the Prophet (ﷺ). Enter the mosque with your right foot, keeping in mind that one prayer here equals 1,000 prayers anywhere else.
madinahPlace2Title: Riyad Al Jannah (The Garden of Paradise)
madinahPlace2Desc: Located inside Masjid An-Nabawi, this is the sacred area situated between the Prophet's grave and his pulpit. It is highly recommended to pray here, as it is a literal piece of Jannah on earth.
madinahPlace3Title: The Grave of the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ)
madinahPlace3Desc: Stand respectfully at the sacred resting place of the Prophet (ﷺ) to send salawat and greetings, ensuring you face the grave itself rather than the Qibla.
madinahPlace3SubTitle: The Graves of Abu Bakr As-Siddiq and Umar Ibn Al-Khattab
madinahPlace3SubDesc: Located inside the Prophet's Mosque complex, move slightly to the right of the Prophet's grave to greet Abu Bakr As-Siddiq (رضي الله عنه), and then step further right to greet Umar Ibn Al-Khattab (رضي الله عنه).
madinahPlace4Desc: The primary graveyard of the companions located immediately adjacent to Masjid An-Nabawi. It is a deeply reflective place to visit and make dua for those buried there.
madinahPlace5Desc: The first masjid ever built in Islamic history. Praying 2 rakats here holds a massive spiritual reward, equivalent to completing an entire Umrah.
madinahPlace6Desc: The historic Mosque of the Two Qiblas, famous as the site where the direction of prayer was divinely shifted from Jerusalem to Mecca.
madinahPlace7Title: Uhud Mountain & The Grave of Hamza (رضي الله عنه)
madinahPlace7Desc: Visit the rugged landscape of the historic Battle of Uhud. Climb the Archers' Hill to view the battlefield and visit the Martyrs' Cemetery to pay respects at the grave of Hamza (رضي الله عنه), the uncle of the Prophet (ﷺ).
madinahPlace8Desc: A cluster of small, historic places of worship located on the western edge of Mount Sela, built near the ancient site of the Battle of the Trench.
madinahPlace9Desc: A heritage museum featuring intricate 3D architectural models and dioramas that track the chronological history and urban expansion of the city and the Prophet's Mosque.
madinahPlace9Sub1Title: The International Fair and Museum of the Prophet's Biography
madinahPlace9Sub1Desc: A state-of-the-art indoor facility right outside the mosque gates that utilizes virtual reality and large-screen projections to bring early Islamic history to life.
madinahPlace9Sub2Desc: Housed inside a beautifully restored Ottoman-era stone terminus, this site showcases historical steam locomotives and classic train cars from the early 20th century.
madinahPlace9Sub3Desc: A peaceful, expansive green park filled with mature date palm groves and walking paths, offering a calm outdoor escape for families during the cooler evening hours.

siteArafahDetail1: Standing here is the heart of Hajj
siteArafahDetail5: Hajj is invalid without this standing

siteHaramDetail3: Safa and Marwah hills are within

siteMinaDesc: A valley near Makkah where pilgrims spend several nights during Hajj. Known as the City of Tents — over 100,000 tents house pilgrims.

siteMinaDetail5: Largest tent city in the world
siteNabawiDesc: The Prophet's Mosque in Madinah was built by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. His tomb is located here — the second holiest site in Islam.
siteNabawiDetail3: Originally built by the Prophet ﷺ
siteNabawiDetail4: Green dome marks the Prophet's tomb
siteSafaDesc: Two hills inside Masjid Al-Haram where pilgrims perform Sa'i — walking 7 times between them, following Hajar's search for water.

siteSafaDetail5: Required for both Umrah and Hajj
siteZamzamDesc: The sacred well inside Masjid Al-Haram. Water miraculously appeared for Hajar and Ismail. Has been flowing for over 4000 years.
